sections.content: You know both forms: *ir a* + infinitive from A1 and the simple future from A2 Unit 19. *Ir a* normally presents an existing intention. The simple future is often more suitable for predictions, expectations or future results. In everyday speech the two often overlap.

items.spanish: Voy a reservar el hotel esta tarde porque ya he elegido las fechas.
items.english: I'm going to book the hotel this afternoon because I've already chosen the dates.

items.spanish: Creo que el hotel será más caro en agosto.
items.english: I think the hotel will be more expensive in August.

items.spanish: Vamos a viajar en tren, aunque todavía no hemos comprado los boletos.
items.english: We're going to travel by train, although we haven't bought the tickets yet.

items.spanish: El viaje será complicado, pero encontraremos una solución.
items.english: The trip will be complicated, but we'll find a solution.

sections.content: A safe guide: use *voy a* + infinitive for something you have already decided (*voy a reservar el hotel*) and the future for a guess (*creo que será más caro*).
